text: John is the company accountant for XYZ. He has recently prepared the annual financial statements
for the company, which show that it has made a significant profit.
John meets his friend Frank for lunch. Frank tells John that he has inherited a large sum of money.
John says that XYZ has had an exceptionally good year and that he believes that the company
will grow and become more profitable every year. Frank invests all his inheritance in XYZ.
The following year XYZ goes out of business. John had not taken into consideration a number
of recent loans obtained by the company when he prepared the financial statements. In fact, the
company was not making a profit but was trading at a loss. However, this was not reflected in the
financial statements prepared by John. Frank has lost his entire investment.
Advise the parties of their rights, responsibilities and potential remedies. [25]
OR
Barchester Council decides to install a charging point for electric vehicles in its main car park. The
council hires Andy, who quotes the lowest price for the work. The council is satisfied that Andy is
knowledgeable and experienced enough as an electrician to do the work, even though he has had
no previous experience of installing vehicle charging points.
Andy completes the installation work, but customers soon start to complain that their vehicles are
not charging properly. Colm, the chairman of the council, uses the charging point to charge his
own car and receives an electric shock, resulting in minor burns. The council contacts a specialist
company to inspect Andy’s work and is advised to close the charging point until it has been
inspected.
Liam, aged 13, goes to the car park. There is a sign on the charging point which says, ‘out of use’.
Nevertheless, Liam uses it to charge his electric scooter, which overheats and catches fire. As he
runs from the car park, he falls and breaks his arm. His electric scooter is destroyed in the fire.
Advise the parties of their rights, responsibilities and potential remedies. [25]
Section B
Answer two questions from this section.
The standard of care in negligence is an objective one. However, in a limited number of
circumstances the court should take into consideration the individual characteristics of the
defendant.
Assess the validity of this statement. [25]
Evaluate the operation of the defence of contributory negligence. [25]
The rule in Rylands v Fletcher is no longer necessary because a remedy can generally be found
in private nuisance.
Assess the validity of this statement. [25]
